title_clean: Best Arbitrage Trade - 25% ROI with 0 Risk!
summary: Builds a hedged carry trade: buy sovereign gold bonds at a ~10% discount to physical gold, pledge them as trading collateral (cash component), short MCX gold futures to remove price risk, and harvest contango roll profits (~31% on the margin deployed).
lessons: Cash-futures arbitrage is mostly dead in India - transaction costs and algo competition eat the spread.
SGB trades at a discount to physical gold and pays 2.5% interest: discount unwind plus interest gives ~4% pre-carry return.
Pledging SGB as collateral (counts as cash component) lets a trader stay invested AND trade on the limit.
Shorting MCX gold futures against SGB removes gold-price risk entirely; contango roll adds extra return each renewal.
This structure works only for derivative traders who need collateral - not a general retail product.

strategies.name: SGB + short MCX gold futures hedged carry
strategies.construction: Buy SGB (e.g. 1kg equivalent ~50L); pledge as collateral; short 1kg MCX gold futures using ~5L of the limit; roll short at each expiry (contracts every 2 months)
strategies.numbers: SGB ~4,800/g vs physical ~5,300/g (~10% discount); GOI interest 2.5%/yr + ~1.5%/yr discount unwind = ~4%; roll spread ~130-150 per 10g per month ~ 1.56L/yr on 5L margin = ~31% ROI; optional overlay: sell 50,000 put @150 (10g) for extra ~3,000/month
strategies.best_regime: When SGB trades at a wide discount and MCX gold is in contango; for F&O traders with collateral requirement
strategies.adjustments: Roll the short future to the next series each expiry; optionally add short put when already short future (no extra margin)
strategies.risks: Roll spread can shrink to near zero; margin calls if gold spikes sharply (temporary MTM); SGB liquidity is limited; interest is taxable at slab rate

title_clean: How 99% Traders Fail - The Typical Journey
summary: Traces the standard failure arc: cash market impatience -> leveraged futures -> social-media advice -> technical-analysis workshop -> overleveraged blowup on a news gap -> overcorrection to tiny size -> tiny portfolio returns. Conclusion: success is margin management, not indicators.
lessons: Technical analysis is part of a trading system, not the heart of it - over-reliance on charts is a failure signature.
Futures are pure leverage: a 1% price move is a ~10% move on margin; novices see only the upside.
In India, gaps make stop-losses unreliable for positional trades - overnight news can blow through any stop.
Overcorrecting to tiny size after a blowup produces 10% return on 20% of capital = 2% portfolio return; ROCE and portfolio return are different things.
Success lies in margin management and position sizing, not in indicator knowledge.
Profit screenshots on social media are marketing funnels for workshops - a 30-crore monthly screenshot with a modest lifestyle is a red flag.
